entry.summary: A Twitter (𝕏) thread was filled with misconceptions about MongoDB, spreading fear, uncertainty, and doubt (FUD). This led one user to question whether MongoDB acknowledges writes before they are actually flushed to disk: Doesn't MongoDB acknowledge writes before it's actually flushed them to disk? MongoDB, like many databases, employs journaling—also known as write-ahead logging (WAL)—to ensure durability (the D in ACID) with high performance. This involves safely recording write operations in the journal, and ensuring they are flushed to disk before the commit is acknowledged. Further details can be found in the documentation under Write Concern and Journaling Here is how you can test it, in a lab, with Linux STRACE and GDB, to debunk the myths.
